title: Verbal Adverbs 4: Prior Completed Action
description: What the perfective verbal adverb means: an action completed BEFORE the main verb. Today: producing the form in real sentences and contrasting it with the imperfective.
descriptionRussian: Что значит совершенное деепричастие: действие, завершённое до главного глагола. Сегодня: употребление формы на -в в реальных предложениях и противопоставление несовершенному виду.
intro: The perfective form means one action finished before the other began. That is the whole distinction from lesson 2, and it maps neatly onto the aspect choice you have been making since A2: overlapping time takes the imperfective, sequence takes the perfective. English needs 'having done' or 'after doing'; Russian needs neither word.
rules: A perfective verbal adverb describes an action completed BEFORE the main verb. The two are sequential, not simultaneous.
The English equivalent is 'having X-ed' or 'after X-ing.' Russian usually does not need the word 'after'; the perfective gerund itself does the work.
If the two actions share a stretch of time, use the imperfective gerund (lesson 2). If one finishes before the other begins, use the perfective gerund.
Like all gerunds, the perfective form must share a subject with the main verb (full treatment in lesson 5).
examples: Прочитав книгу, она лежала на диване. (Having read the book, she lay on the sofa.)
Услышав новость, Антон позвонил маме. (Having heard the news, Anton called his mom.)
Вернувшись домой, Лена легла спать. (Having returned home, Lena went to bed.)
Открыв окно, я почувствовал холодный ветер. (Having opened the window, I felt the cold wind.)
Сказав 'спасибо', Маша вышла. (Having said thanks, Masha went out.)
Узнав правду, Иван улыбнулся. (Having learned the truth, Ivan smiled.)

items.prompt: Recap from L3: what is the perfective verbal adverb of написать?
items.hint: Drop -ть from the perfective infinitive. Add the suffix.
items.explanation: Recap from L3: написать → написа- + в → написав. Написал is the finite past; написать is the infinitive; писав is not standard for either aspect of this pair.

items.promptEnglish: Having read the book, she went to bed.
items.hint: The reading is finished BEFORE the going to bed. Which form expresses a prior completed action?
items.explanation: Прочитав is the perfective gerund and signals that the book was finished before she went to bed. Читая would mean she went to bed WHILE reading, a different sequence; прочитать is the infinitive; читала is the imperfective finite past.

items.promptEnglish: Having heard the music, Ivan started dancing.
items.hint: The hearing happens first; the dancing comes after. Which form fits?
items.explanation: Услышав is the perfective gerund of услышать (drop -ть, add -в). It marks the hearing as completed before the dancing starts. Слушая would mean Ivan dances while listening, a simultaneous reading; услышать is the infinitive; услышал is the finite past.

items.promptEnglish: Pick the perfective verbal adverb of вернуться.
items.hint: Reflexive perfective verbs add -вшись, keeping the reflexive marker.
items.explanation: Вернувшись is the perfective gerund of reflexive вернуться (-ться → -вшись). Возвращаясь is the imperfective gerund of возвращаться (the aspect partner, simultaneous reading); вернулся is the finite past; вернуть is the non-reflexive infinitive (a different verb).

items.promptEnglish: Having opened the door, Masha saw the guests.
items.hint: The door is opened BEFORE she sees the guests. Which gerund fits?
items.explanation: Открыв (perfective gerund of открыть) marks the door-opening as completed before the seeing. Открывая ('while opening') would mean she sees the guests during the opening motion, a different reading; открыть is the infinitive; открыла is finite past.

items.prompt: Pick the sentence whose gerund signals an action that happened BEFORE the main verb.
items.promptEnglish: Which sentence uses a perfective gerund (prior completed action)?
options: Гуляя по парку, мы говорили о работе.
Зная город, она нашла дорогу легко.
items.hint: Imperfective gerunds end in -я / -а; perfective gerunds end in -в / -вшись. Which option uses a perfective form?
items.explanation: Сказав is a perfective gerund (-в ending) describing the saying as completed before the leaving. The other three options use imperfective gerunds (гуляя, зная, сидя), which describe simultaneous action and belong to lesson 2.

items.promptEnglish: Having opened the door, Masha stepped out into the street.
items.hint: The door-opening completes before the stepping out.
items.explanation: A prior completed action takes the perfective gerund: Открыв дверь, Маша вышла. Открывая would keep the door mid-opening while she walks; the finite past cannot head the clause.

items.promptEnglish: Having heard the news, Anton called his mom.
items.explanation: The hearing completes first, so the perfective gerund: Услышав новость, Антон позвонил маме. Слыша would run the hearing alongside the call; finite forms cannot open the clause.

items.promptEnglish: Having returned home, Lena went to bed.
items.hint: A reflexive perfective gerund: which ending?
items.explanation: Reflexive perfective verbs take -вшись: Вернувшись домой, Лена легла спать. Возвращаясь would keep her mid-journey; the finite past and infinitive cannot head the gerund clause.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Perfective verbal adverb expresses an action completed before the main verb. Reflexive verbs take -вшись.
hints: Returning happens first; going to bed comes after. Which form expresses a prior completed action of a reflexive verb?
explanations: Вернувшись is the perfective gerund of reflexive вернуться. The return is completed before the bedtime. Возвращаясь is the imperfective gerund of возвращаться ('while returning,' a simultaneous reading); вернулась is the finite past; вернуться is the infinitive.

errorCorrection.sentence: Видя гостей, Маша улыбнулась и открыла дверь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having seen the guests, Masha smiled and opened the door.
errorCorrection.explanation: The gloss 'having seen the guests, ... smiled and opened' is a two-step sequence: the seeing completes, then the reactions follow, which calls for the perfective gerund увидев. Видя is the imperfective ('while seeing'), which frames an ongoing background instead.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having learned the truth, Masha smiled.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Having learned the truth, Masha smiled' is sequential: first she learns it, then she smiles, so the slot needs the perfective gerund узнав. Узнавая is the imperfective gerund of узнавать ('while finding out'), which would mean the smiling happened during an ongoing process of learning, not after a completed discovery. Узная uses the imperfective -я on the perfective stem and is not standard, and Узнавши is the obsolete -вши variant. Because the learning completes before the smile, узнав is correct.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having had breakfast, Ivan went to work.
errorCorrection.explanation: Breakfast is finished before the leaving starts, so the perfective gerund позавтракав fits, formed by dropping -ть and adding -в. Позавтракавши is the archaic long variant, out of place in neutral modern prose. Завтракая would mean 'while having breakfast'.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Reading the book, he drank tea.
minimalPairs.explanation: The reading and the tea-drinking happen together; both unfold over the same stretch of time. The imperfective Читая carries the simultaneous reading. Прочитав ('having read') would imply he finished the book first, then drank tea, a different sequence.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Having read the book, he went to bed.
minimalPairs.explanation: The reading is finished BEFORE he goes to bed; the two actions are sequential. The perfective Прочитав fits. Читая would mean he goes to bed while still reading, which the sentence does not support.

reviewVocab.definition: before (the timing relation expressed by a perfective verbal adverb: the gerund's action happens before the main verb's)
reviewVocab.example: Прочитав книгу, она пошла спать — чтение до того, как она легла.

reviewVocab.definition: after (the same relation seen from the other side: the main verb happens after the gerund's action)
reviewVocab.example: После чтения она пошла спать = Прочитав книгу, она пошла спать.

reviewVocab.definition: perfective verbal adverb (-в / -вшись; expresses prior completed action; built from the perfective infinitive by dropping -ть)
reviewVocab.example: Услышав, прочитав, вернувшись — все это совершенные деепричастия.

reviewVocab.definition: imperfective verbal adverb (-я / -а; expresses simultaneous action; the contrast partner of the perfective form)
reviewVocab.example: Слушая, читая, возвращаясь — все это несовершенные деепричастия.
